hints: Only two products contribute to $x^3$: the constant $3$ times the cubic term, and $-x$ times the quadratic term of the binomial expansion.
Use the general binomial coefficients for $(1+3x)^{1/3}$ to write its $x^2$ and $x^3$ terms explicitly.
Form $3[\text{coefficient of }x^3]-[\text{coefficient of }x^2]$ and simplify; report the coefficient, not the whole term.
walkthrough:
State the binomial expansion formula for $(1 + u)^n$:
$$(1 + u)^n = 1 + nu + \dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}u^2 + \dfrac{n(n - 1)(n - 2)}{3!}u^3 + \dots$$

Apply this expansion to $(1 + 3x)^{\frac{1}{3}}$ with $n = \dfrac{1}{3}$ and $u = 3x$:
- First term: $1$
- Second term ($x^1$):
$$\dfrac{1}{3}(3x) = x$$
- Third term ($x^2$):
$$\dfrac{\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{1}{3} - 1\right)}{2}(3x)^2 = \dfrac{\frac{1}{3}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)}{2}(9x^2) = \dfrac{-\frac{2}{9}}{2}(9x^2) = -x^2$$
- Fourth term ($x^3$):
$$\dfrac{\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{1}{3} - 1\right)\left(\frac{1}{3} - 2\right)}{6}(3x)^3 = \dfrac{\frac{1}{3}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right)}{6}(27x^3) = \dfrac{\frac{10}{27}}{6}(27x^3) = \dfrac{10}{6}x^3 = \dfrac{5}{3}x^3$$

Write out the series expansion of $(1 + 3x)^{\frac{1}{3}}$ up to $x^3$:
$$(1 + 3x)^{\frac{1}{3}} = 1 + x - x^2 + \dfrac{5}{3}x^3 + \dots$$

Multiply the series by $(3 - x)$:
$$(3 - x)(1 + 3x)^{\frac{1}{3}} = (3 - x)\left(1 + x - x^2 + \dfrac{5}{3}x^3 + \dots\right)$$

Extract all terms producing $x^3$:
- From $3 \times \left(\dfrac{5}{3}x^3\right)$:
$$3 \times \dfrac{5}{3}x^3 = 5x^3$$
- From $(-x) \times (-x^2)$:
$$(-x)(-x^2) = +x^3$$

Add the two contributions to obtain the total $x^3$ term:
$$\text{Term in } x^3 = 5x^3 + x^3 = 6x^3$$
$$\text{Coefficient of } x^3 = 6$$

ai_rubric.Finding Coefficients in Expansions: Identifies the unsimplified term in $x^2$, or its coefficient, in $(1+3x)^{1/3}$: $\dfrac{(1/3)(-2/3)}2(3x)^2$. Multiplies by $(3-x)$ to give two terms in $x^3$, or the displayed coefficients. Gives $6$. The final result is $6$.
